Samantha / DataCo infra —

Attached is a compact Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and our benchmarking runbook. Highlighting the key milestones and owners below so procurement and infra can move this through:

MAP summary (high level):
- Day 0 (Oct 15): Redwood to provide ephemeral test API key and instructions; DataCo to confirm network rules (security group, peering)
- Day 1 (Oct 18): Smoke tests + connectivity validation (20–30 min)
- Day 2 (Oct 19): Controlled sustained run: 30 minute steady state with 5 minute ramp up / ramp down; target concurrency: 120 sessions
- Day 3 (Oct 20): Optional extended run for cost/throughput profiling (1–2 hours)

Evaluation plan / success criteria:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median target <= 200 ms
- End-to-end latency (100-token generation): p50 <= 700 ms, p95 <= 1.5 s
- Sustained throughput: baseline target >= 1,500 tokens/sec across the cluster for 30m
- Concurrency: sustain 120 concurrent sessions with graceful degradation beyond 180 sessions

Logistics notes:
- We will generate a temporary API key and a separate read-only test account for your engineers. See attached access_keys_readme.txt for instructions.
- Please confirm an IP range for the VPC peering; we need firewall openings on TCP 443 to our public gateway and peering subnet for private tests.
- Karthik (ccd) will own the run execution; Marissa will be on-call for anomaly triage.

Next steps:
1) Confirm the Oct 18 smoke window and who will be on the call
2) DataCo provides ephemeral test key request via the form in the attachment
3) Redwood schedules the load window on our ops calendar (we'll reserve capacity)

If that looks good Ill update the MAP spreadsheet and share a final Doc.

Thanks,

Samantha / DataCo infra —

Appended is the short benchmarking report and an updated MAP marking deliverables complete for the evaluation phase. Summary of the controlled runs executed on Oct 19 (10:00–12:00 PST):

Test configuration (short):
- Model: rwft-13b-quant (sequence 1024 sampling; sampling temperature 0.2)
- Cluster: 4x A100-p4d nodes (quantized serving path), continuous batching enabled
- Workload: 30 minute steady state after 5 minute ramp; synthetic user traces derived from your sample prompts
- Observability: per-request traces, token-level latency, and throughput export (CSV attached)

Key results (observed):
- Median TTFT (time-to-first-token): 0.13 s (130 ms)
- Median per-token latency: 0.012 s/token (12 ms/token)
- End-to-end generation latency (100-token response): p50 = 0.72 s, p95 = 1.18 s, p99 = 1.9 s
- Sustained cluster throughput: 2,150 tokens/sec (30m window, standard deviation 120 tokens/sec)
- Concurrency sustained without SLA breach: 180 concurrent sessions; graceful degradation observed above 220 sessions
- Cost proxy (post-run): estimated incremental infra cost $0.027 per 1k tokens for this configuration

Interpretation and next steps:
- The observed p95 of 1.18 s meets the stated SLA target of <= 1.5 s. TTFT is well below the 200 ms threshold.
- If DataCo needs lower p99 at larger concurrency, we recommend either (a) adding an additional A100 node to the cluster for burst capacity, or (b) using a lighter model variant for high-concurrency endpoints.
- We exported the trace CSV and included a short appendix in the attached PDF with failure-mode notes (resets during warmup, network tail spikes).

Action items closed:
- Redwood provided ephemeral key and read-only test account (see access_keys_readme.txt)
- Connectivity validated and smoke tests passed Oct 18
- Controlled sustained run executed Oct 19; report attached

Proposed closure for evaluation phase: sign-off by DataCo infra (Samantha) and procurement ok for Dedicated reservation if you want to move forward. If youd like, we can schedule a wrap-up call next week to walk the report with your platform team.

Thanks everyone — great collaboration.

— Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
